name.en: Fake police detective: “your crypto wallet is at risk”

how.en: A caller says they are a police detective and that your details or ID were found on someone who was arrested. They ask whether and how you hold cryptocurrency, then pass you to a fake “representative” of your crypto company. That person gets you to hand over your passwords or seed phrase, often on a fake page that looks like the real app. Police say victims have lost millions, and scammers can spoof real police phone numbers and emails.

text.en: A “detective” calls, saying your details were found on someone arrested.
They ask whether you hold cryptocurrency and where.
A fake representative of your crypto company contacts you.
They get your password or seed phrase, often on a fake page, and empty the wallet.

This is Detective Sergeant Morgan from NZ Police. Your driver licence was found on a man we arrested this morning and we believe your crypto account is at risk. Someone from your exchange will call you shortly to secure it.

en: my id found on someone arrested
Police asking about crypto wallets, bank cards, PINs, seed phrases or passwords. They never do on a call.
A second caller “from your exchange” right after the police call.
A web page asking for your seed phrase.
A caller ID that looks like a real police number (it can be spoofed).
Never share your seed phrase or passwords, and never type your seed phrase into a website.
Ask for the officer’s details, hang up and call 105 to check.
If you shared anything, contact your crypto exchange straight away.

sources.title: Police warn of scammers impersonating NZ Police targeting cryptocurrency wallet holders
Scammers impersonating police to target victims for cryptocurrency theft
